description:
I've been fiddling about with the game. It's fun to break open files, edit values or swap/insert lines of code and see what happens, because sometimes genuinely interesting or cool things can be the result. This is a compilation of working alterations I've discovered. Thought I would share them with you all.

I'll be writing up some handwritten guides on how to do things, as time goes on. Most edits require digging into the .jar files and making changes using external tools such as Recaf or PowerShell and/or mods like Microforge. There could be some other more simple edits or "normal" mods too. Doubtful, but we'll see.

As a note, I have used ChatGPT to help me along the way. It's a great soundboard for ideas I might have, confirming whether or not they are possible within the confines of the code, checking I haven't made mistakes with my alterations, etc. Also because I'm not manually looking through thousands of lines of code for a single value to alter. It has better eyesight than me for finding things!

The edits are done by hand, though. Makes it easier to build guides that way. Learn by doing and all that.

The file alterations have been tested multiple times, both during and after creation. Firstly, GPT ran the code within itself to ensure there were no conflicts or incorrect values and that the alterations I made worked. Then I tested everything in-game and ran roughly 6-12 months (depending on what was changed), in case there were unintended effects. This is how I ironed-out any issues. I couldn't see any in the final versions, but I won't stand on a soap box and shout

"How dare you! They are perfect and you're doing it wrong!"

because games are fickle at the best of times.

You'll need some extra bits and pieces, as listed in the guides.

If you want to stack these edits on top of each other, then use an already-edited .jar file from another edit, in place of the vanilla one(s) in the guide. I've done this, to have all changes together in one game and it works perfectly fine.

I'll continue to alter the first post as I discover and construct them. Bookmark the page, if you wish to check for updates now and again. I don't want to keep bumping this to the top through individual comments, but sometimes I'll get overstimulated about a successful edit and find it hard to resist the urge to tell someone. I'm excitable, sorry about that. It won't be unnecessary or targeted bumping, at least.

Devs and users are welcome to use and/or butcher anything I create for their own purposes. If something I've done means it has helped anybody in some way, I'm happy to have contributed towards that.

A simple thanks is enough.

So, without further ado.

RANDOM GUIDES FOR VARIOUS GAME CHANGES:

Click the titles for links to Pastebin guides.

Thicker Campaign Map Circles

Increases the thickness of the circles that surround fleets, stations, derelicts and such on the System and Hyperspace maps.

Works with all factions, vanilla and modded. Takes the colours directly from the .faction files.

This scales as you zoom in and out. Zoom in, the circles become thinner and vice versa. Fully customisable thickness, through simple value edits.

Spoiler[close]

Commission-Based UI Colour Schemes

The colour of the player's campaign map circles and UI will dynamically change, depending on what faction they have a Commission with.

For example, if you take a Hegemony Commission, the circles and UI will change to the faction's orange colour scheme. If you resign the Commission, it will automatically revert back to the standard grey (or whatever colour you have changed it to, in the player.faction file). Grab a new Commission, even with a different faction, it changes again!

It uses whatever RGBA values are present in the .faction files, so if you have altered any faction colour schemes (as I have), it will automatically display those colours. No trickery involved, just pointing it in the right direction. Works with all factions, vanilla and modded.

Improved Scan and Survey Missions

Modifies the starting location of missions to the market/system that generated them.

The vanilla game will always calculate the credit reward earned from the 0,0 centre of the sector outwards. So if you take a mission from a system that is in, say, the bottom-left corner and the mission target is in the top-right corner, the code does not take into account the fact that you have to travel across the entire map. You will only be paid as if you were starting your journey from the centre.

Logically, that didn't make sense to me, so this edit changes that calculation. Now the faction market from the system who spawns a mission will be the starting location and the reward calculated properly from there instead. You'll be paid appropriately for the entire journey, from source to target. No more being cheated out of credits!

Also includes some extra information on how to edit the mission completion time limit, credit rewards and faction reputation changes.

Hyperspace Nebulae Layers

Adds three moving layers of nebulae to the Hyperspace map. Also disables the "wobble" effect from the Hyperspace map.

The nebulae sprites are taken from the existing image present in the graphics\terrain folder. No new assets have been added at all. Just some clever code to say "use this image, chop it up, do this and that, put them on this layer in this manner", all using proper coding.

Each layer uses different speeds, sizes and seeding, to create truly unique nebulae layers. This creates a wonderful moving background nebula effect, as you travel through Hyperspace.

You can see the effect in motion, from the video in the spoiler below.

Spoiler[close]

Removal of the wobble effect, I would say is necessary. You won't see it, so there is no point in keeping it around. There is an optional (but recommended) custom background image, that I made from the sprites and darkened, to use as the Hyperspace background for those times when it

might

peek through.

As a note, when you zoom in and out, it does go a bit weird as it rearranges the layers to match the zoom level. That can't be avoided. I'll look into it again, but I couldn't figure out how to stop it. If you have any ideas, please feel free to comment about it.
